Making Tax Digital for Income Tax from 6 April 2027: incomes over £30,000

Who starts in April 2027 and when the quarterly updates are due

Sole traders and landlords with qualifying income over £30,000 in the 2025 to 2026 tax year use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax from 6 April 2027. You cannot file Income Tax with Submit yet. VAT returns are filed today: see VAT return from a spreadsheet.

Who starts on 6 April 2027

The rule covers sole traders and landlords who are registered for Self Assessment, when their qualifying income is over £30,000.

Source: GOV.UK, Find out if and when you need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax (checked 13 November 2026)

Quarterly updates

Send an update for each quarter by its deadline. These are the standard update periods.

Update periods and deadlines
Update period Deadline
6 April to 5 July 7 August
6 April to 5 October 7 November
6 April to 5 January 7 February
6 April to 5 April 7 May, in the following tax year
Source: GOV.UK, Use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - Send quarterly updates - Guidance (checked 13 November 2026)

Final declaration

The tax return for the year follows the quarterly updates.

You must submit your tax return by 31 January after the end of the relevant tax year, but you can submit it earlier.

Source: GOV.UK, Use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - Submit your tax return - Guidance (checked 22 November 2026)

What Submit files

Submit files VAT returns now. See VAT return from a spreadsheet.

The dates for other income levels, and for every other filing, are on the MTD calendar.

You cannot file Income Tax (MTD) with Submit yet. This page will say when you can. Until then, use software from HMRC's list.
